# Explore an Environment

Make sure an Environment is ready, open a deployed Service, and use Lifecycle's pull request comments.

After Lifecycle deploys your first Environment, make sure that its Services are
ready before you start testing. You can examine the Environment in the
Lifecycle UI and use the comments on your pull request to change or monitor it.

## Make sure that the Environment is ready

1. Follow the **View details** link in the Lifecycle comment, or open
   **Environments** in Lifecycle and select your Environment.
2. Make sure that the Environment status is **Deployed**.
3. Select each Service you plan to test. A correctly deployed Service shows
   **Ready** and the message **Kubernetes pods are ready**.
4. Select **Visit URL** to open a public Service.

![Environment details with Deployed status and a web Service with Ready status.](/docs/getting-started/explore-environment/environment-ready.png)

If a Service shows **Build failed**, **Deploy failed**, or **Error**, open its
**Console**. See [Troubleshoot a failed
deployment](/docs/troubleshooting/deploy-issues) for the recovery workflow.

## Test your application

Open a deployed public Service from **Visit URL** or from the pull request
comment, then:

1. Test the smallest user path that shows the deployed change.
2. Make sure that calls to each necessary backend or dependency succeed.
3. Check only non-secret runtime configuration through a surface your
   application intentionally exposes.
4. Go back to Lifecycle to examine a different Service or its logs.

## Use the Mission Control comment

Lifecycle's editable pull-request comment is the GitHub control surface for the
Environment. It can contain:

- **Service checkboxes:** Select or deselect optional Services.
- **Branch or external URL values:** Change the source used for an eligible
  Service.
- **Environment ID and variable overrides:** Apply changes to this Environment
  without editing the repository configuration.
- **Actions:** Queue a redeploy and run other configured operations.
- **Options:** Change conditional settings that the installation exposes.

> [!NOTE]
> Lifecycle parses the comment as product input. Its headings and syntax control
> the parsed values. The [Mission Control comment
> reference](/docs/tips/using-mission-control) has correct examples.

## Follow status updates

Lifecycle adds status comments by default. It updates them when the Environment
status changes. An operator can turn that repository default off. If the
operator turns it off, apply the configured status-comment label.

Use the status comment to see:

- Current Environment changes
- Each Service's current status
- Available build-log links from the deployment backend

Operators can change the default label names. See
[Configurable labels](/docs/features/configurable-labels) before you write
automation that uses a literal label.

and try selecting one optional Service from your own configuration.
